source_wording: Continuous functions can be approximated by smooth functions.
domain_and_universes: Open: a finite-dimensional smooth manifold M, a scalar codomain or smooth target manifold N, and the relevant universe and model-space parameters must be selected in the statement phase.
quantifiers: a smooth manifold M (and, for the map-valued form, a smooth manifold N)
a continuous function or map f
an approximation tolerance or neighborhood of f, depending on the selected topology
possibly a closed subset on which f is already smooth
hypotheses: the precise manifold regularity, countability, paracompactness, and boundary assumptions
the chosen approximation topology and tolerance data
relative smoothness assumptions if a relative form is selected
conclusion: Open choice among uniform or pointwise smooth approximation of scalar functions, approximation of manifold-valued maps, and the associated smooth-homotopy or relative conclusion.
statement_choices_requiring_source_audit: scalar-valued function versus map between smooth manifolds
uniform, compact-open, strong/Whitney, or pointwise positive-tolerance approximation
approximation alone versus existence of a homotopic smooth map
absolute versus relative approximation near a closed subset
manifolds with or without boundary and finite differentiability versus C-infinity
boundary_and_exclusions: No density claim in an unspecified function-space topology
No embedding or immersion theorem is included merely because it is also due to Whitney
No relative or fixed-on-a-subset conclusion is credited until its hypotheses are sourced
No arbitrary topological source or target substitutes for a smooth-manifold theorem

WA-REL preservation near a closed subset when selected
WA-HOM construction of a homotopy when selected
